newsitem.title: MALAWI: STATE-OWNED MALAWIAN INSURANCE FIRM TO GO PUBLIC.
newsitem.headline: STATE-OWNED MALAWIAN INSURANCE FIRM TO GO PUBLIC.

text.p: The Malawi Development Corporation (MDC) is to sell most of its 20 percent stake in the state-owned National Insurance Company Ltd -- a move seen as the first major development in the country's privatisation process.

Stockbrokers Malawi Ltd said in a statement that a total of 13-million shares of US$0.13 each would be sold, six million of which would be offered to the general public and four million to Malawian citizens at a discount.
In terms of the country's privatisation laws, shares bought at a discount are not to be resold within two years after purchase.
Two million of the shares would be offered to the company's employees, while one million of the shares would be offered at a preferential rate.
Following the sale, MDC's stake would be reduced to five percent.

Former president Kamuzu Banda's Press Corporation -- the country's largest conglomerate -- would retain its 54.9 percent stake as would South Africa's Guardian National Insurance, which holds a 25.1 percent stake.
Further details of the offer would be announced on September 27 when the company released its prospectus ahead of its listing on the Malawian Stock Exchange.

In a separate development, the Malawian government announced on Thursday that it had set aside nearly $670,000 in a special fund for loans to citizens whose income was below $670 a month for buying shares on offer.
